do_not_assume: Attribute inheritance means every setting is inherited.
A role named Leader has `Is Leader` enabled.
A valid hierarchy works with the Attendance Digest.
goal: A bounded Group Type design with explicit hierarchy, roles, attributes, and security.
steps: Inventory existing Group Types and look for a reusable common type before proposing another.
Define whether the tree is structured or flexible.
List allowed child types at every level.
Define roles and mark only genuine leader roles as `Is Leader`.
Assign role capabilities for viewing, editing, member management, attendance, and check-in.
Place shared attributes on the base type and specialized attributes on the specialized type.
Define schedule modes, location options, history, requirements, sync, and security.
Test creation at every intended hierarchy level.
title: Recipe: Design a Group Type and hierarchy

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: An intended group is discoverable without exposing unnecessary location precision.
steps: Confirm the group is active and public.
Confirm its Group Type is included in the finder.
Configure an appropriate location and privacy precision.
Use a Weekly schedule if visitors must filter by day or time.
Review capacity and the block’s overcapacity behavior.
Confirm the detail and registration linked pages.
Test initial load, each enabled filter, map behavior, details, and registration as an anonymous visitor.
If seasonal, test closed-state routes, redirects, blocks, and alternate surfaces.
Confirm the group is marked `Public`.
Confirm its Group Type is included in the block’s configured Group Types.
Check whether the group has reached capacity and whether overcapacity groups are hidden.
Inspect location-type, campus, geofence, and attribute filters.
If filtering by day or time, confirm the group uses a Weekly schedule.
Test the public route and any alternate or mobile surface as an anonymous visitor.
title: Recipe: Publish a group through Group Finder

do_not_assume: Every group has a usable location or schedule.
Every Rapid Attendance Entry page exposes the same actions.
A visible workflow button proves that the workflow completed successfully.
goal: Ministry staff can enter attendance and only the related actions appropriate to that workflow.
steps: Select the target Group and attendance date.
Confirm the valid location and schedule context.
Review which related actions are needed: family changes, new family members, notes, prayer requests, or workflows.
Enable only those actions in the block settings.
Create separate page variants where ministries require different action sets.
Confirm operator permissions.
Test a representative attendance occurrence and read back the saved state.
title: Recipe: Configure focused attendance entry

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Leaders receive the intended reminders, digests, or absence notifications without duplicate or misrouted messages.
steps: Choose the operational mechanism: reminder, digest, absence notification, or attendance-report attributes.
Confirm the Group Type’s attendance settings and leader roles.
For a digest, construct the required parent-region-attendance hierarchy and use Weekly schedules.
Configure the correct System Communication and date or absence settings.
Verify the job scope and cadence.
Run a bounded test using non-production delivery controls where available.
Inspect job results, occurrences, recipient selection, and duplicate-suppression state.
title: Recipe: Configure attendance follow-up

do_not_assume: Manual-add enforcement applies to workflow additions.
A requirement applies to every role or age when selectors narrow it.
A leader receives notifications merely because the role is named Leader.
goal: The intended population is evaluated and manual additions are blocked or overrideable according to policy.
steps: Open the Group Type’s Group Requirements section.
Select the requirement.
Scope it by role, age classification, and Data View as needed.
Decide whether leaders may override it.
Enable pre-add enforcement when required.
Test an eligible and ineligible manual addition.
Inspect every workflow or integration that can add members and implement a separate eligibility check there.
Configure notification recipients and the requirement-notification job if needed.
title: Recipe: Enforce a Group Type requirement

goal: Membership for one role follows a reviewed population rule at a sustainable cadence.
steps: Enable Group Sync on the Group Type.
Create and validate the source Data View.
Add the sync to the target group.
Choose one assigned role.
Set the lowest operationally acceptable frequency.
Review welcome, exit, and login-creation options.
Configure another sync only if another role needs independent management.
Run the Group Sync job and reconcile Data View results with resulting membership.
For communication lists, refresh and reconcile immediately before an authorized send.
Inspect workflow action order and logs.
Check whether membership, communications, or attributes changed before the failure.
Identify which action actually failed.
Make retry logic account for already-completed side effects.
Stop before retrying if duplicate membership, duplicate communication, or repeated downstream actions remain possible.
title: Recipe: Synchronize a group from a Data View

do_not_assume: Blank direct `Manage Members` rules mean no one can manage members.
Group administrator designation grants leader security.
Toolbox navigation limits replace entity security.
goal: Leaders can perform approved group tasks without unnecessary database or group-administration access.
steps: Inspect Group Type security.
Inspect parent-group and direct-group security.
Review the leader role’s capabilities.
Separate `Manage Members` from Edit or Administrate access.
Inspect Group Toolbox block settings and page security.
Decide whether the default People search is appropriate.
If not, configure an alternate controlled add-member path.
Test viewing, editing, roster management, attendance, and navigation as a representative leader.
title: Recipe: Secure leader operations

do_not_assume: Do not infer that missing history means no changes occurred before history was enabled.
goal: Group changes are snapshotted and a retired group is recoverable.
steps: Confirm the Group Type is stable enough for retained history.
Enable Group History on the Group Type.
Confirm the Process Group History job runs successfully.
Inspect the group timeline and member history.
Archive the group instead of deleting it.
Confirm it is absent from normal group-viewer surfaces.
Record the restoration path through Archived Groups.
Confirm **Enable Group History** is enabled on the Group Type.
Confirm the Process Group History job has run successfully since enablement.
Reopen the group after the job completes.
If restoring an archived group, use `Admin Tools > Settings > General > Archived Groups`.
Do not infer that missing history means no changes occurred before history was enabled.
title: Recipe: Enable history and archive a group

do_not_assume: Matching attribute labels mean matching keys.
A successful workflow means every per-person move succeeded.
A draft community recipe is production-ready.
goal: Selected memberships move without unexpected loss of notes or attributes.
steps: Confirm the exact source and destination groups.
Compare destination roles and capacity.
Compare Group Member Attribute keys.
Record values that will not transfer.
Decide whether member notes should move.
Move a representative member.
Verify the destination membership, role, status, notes, and retained attributes.
For bulk automation, add idempotency and per-person verification before scaling.
Confirm Group Sync is enabled for the Group Type.
Inspect the exact Data View result.
Inspect the role assigned by each sync definition.
Compare active group membership with the Data View population.
Check both the group sync interval and the Group Sync job’s latest execution.
Review overlapping syncs, manual memberships, and optional exit behavior.
Before a communication, refresh and reconcile the intended source count using locally reviewed procedures.
title: Recipe: Move group members safely
